mission.setup: Smarty wants to know about your imaginary home. Describe it with new, old, clean, dirty or beautiful.

turns.smarty: Is your house new or old?
turns.hint: Say My house is new. or My house is old.

turns.smarty: Is your bedroom clean or dirty?
turns.hint: Say It is clean. or It is dirty.

turns.smarty: What is beautiful in your house?
turns.hint: Say My... is beautiful. Use a room or a furniture word.

lessons.title: Open the door
lessons.scenario: Tom comes to visit Lily. Give simple instructions to a friend at your door.

items.note: Use 'open' to ask someone to open something. 'Open' starts the sentence. Opens: He opens the door.

image.describe: Mia pulls a front door wide open so you can see a bright room inside; Smarty the black cat sits on the doorstep.

items.note: Use 'close' to ask someone to close something. Closes: She closes the door.

image.describe: Ben pushes a front door shut with his hand; the door is almost closed and Smarty the black cat watches from the floor.

items.note: Say 'stand up' when you want someone to get up from a chair.

image.describe: Sam stands up from a chair with a happy face; his chair is behind him and Smarty the black cat is beside him.

items.note: Say 'come in' to invite someone inside.

practice.prompt: Mia is at your door. You want her to enter. What do you say?
practice.explanation: Come in invites someone inside.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the sentence you heard.
practice.explanation: Listen for the first word: open.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence in the right word order.
practice.explanation: Close + the + thing + please.

practice.prompt: You want the door to be shut. Complete the sentence.
practice.explanation: Close means shut.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud. You can try again if the app mishears you.
practice.explanation: Please makes an instruction polite.

practice.prompt: Ben opens the door for you. What do you say?
practice.explanation: Say Thank you when someone helps you.

practice.prompt: Match each word with its opposite.
practice.explanation: Open and close are opposites.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the sentence you heard.
practice.audio: Stand up and come in, please.
practice.answer: Stand up and come in, please.
options: Stand up and come in, please.
Stand up and close the door, please.
Stand up and open the window, please.
practice.explanation: Listen for both instructions: stand up, come in.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence in the right word order.
practice.answer: Can you open the window, please?
practice.explanation: Can you... is a polite way to ask.

image.describe: Tom stands at Lily's front door on a cold day while Lily waves him in. Smarty the black cat sits in the hallway.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Hello, Lily! Can I come in?

questions.explanation: Lily says: Yes, come in, Tom!

questions.prompt: What does Lily ask Tom to close?
questions.explanation: Lily says: Close the door, please.
Tom answers Lily with: Of course.

mission.setup: Smarty comes to your door. Invite him in, ask him to close the door, and answer him.

turns.smarty: Hello! I am at the door.
turns.hint: Invite Smarty inside: Come in!

turns.smarty: Thank you! It is cold.
turns.hint: Ask for the door to be closed: Close the door, please.

turns.smarty: Can you open the window, please?
turns.hint: Say Of course. or Yes.

lessons.title: Welcome home
lessons.scenario: Mia welcomes Smarty to her home. Show your own imaginary home and say where you live.

items.note: Say 'Welcome' to be friendly when someone comes to your home.
Your 'home' is the place where you live.

image.describe: A cosy house with a red door, a small garden gate and a warm light in the window; Smarty the black cat sits on the doorstep.

items.note: Use 'live' for the place you stay every day. With he, she or a name, say lives.

items.example: I live on a big street.
items.note: A street is a road with houses on it. We say 'on a street'.

image.describe: A quiet street with houses on both sides and a few trees; Smarty the black cat walks along the pavement.

practice.prompt: A friend comes to your home. What do you say?
practice.explanation: Welcome is a friendly greeting for guests.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the sentence you heard.
practice.explanation: Listen for the place after I live in.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence in the right word order.
practice.explanation: Where do you live? asks about your home.

practice.prompt: Complete the sentence about a road with houses.
practice.explanation: We say on a street.

practice.prompt: Match each question with its answer.
practice.explanation: Live is about where you stay. From is about where you were born or where you come from.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud. You can try again if the app mishears you.
practice.explanation: You greeted someone at home.

practice.prompt: Complete the sentence about Sam.
practice.explanation: With a name, use lives.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose the sentence you heard.
practice.explanation: Listen for the last word: house.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence in the right word order.
practice.answer: My family lives in a house.
practice.explanation: Family is one group, so use lives.
